dedupe_keys.name: in core interdependent networked community resilience modeling environment

description: IN-CORE is a computational environment for modelling the impact of natural hazards on whole communities and their recovery. It was built by the Center of Excellence for Risk-Based Community Resilience Planning, funded by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) from 2015 and led by Colorado State University with partner universities, and is hosted by NCSA at the University of Illinois. Users set up interdependent models of buildings, transportation, water and electric power networks, people, businesses and social institutions, apply earthquake, tsunami, hurricane, flood or tornado scenarios, and chain physical damage, loss of functionality, restoration and social and economic impacts with uncertainty propagation. The platform consists of web services with integrated databases of hazards, fragility curves and testbed inventories, the pyIncore Python package (analyses, service clients, visualisation; version 1.22.0, MPL-2.0), a web interface and Jupyter environments. NIST states that IN-CORE is open source and that an account is free; source code is on GitHub and packages on PyPI and anaconda.org. Caveats: the curated datasets and testbeds are US-centred, detailed analyses need considerable input preparation, and the hosted service requires registration. Uses are resilience and recovery analysis, cascading failure across interdependent lifelines, emergency response and investment planning; it hosts fragility models comparable to those used by HAZUS and complements CLIMADA and OpenQuake.

notes: Audit 2026-09-24: re-read on tools.in-core.org (home page, manual introduction and account pages, rendered in Chromium because the site is a JavaScript application; incore.ncsa.illinois.edu redirects there), the pyincore README, LICENSE and CHANGELOG, PyPI, the anaconda.org package API and git tags. Corrections to round 1: the Center of Excellence is headquartered at Colorado State University, not 'hosted by NCSA' (NCSA hosts the platform); supported hazards include flood and combined wind, wave and surge, not only earthquake, tornado and hurricane; the Memphis (MMSA, Shelby County) testbed was missing; platform version 6.3.0 and the six web services added. Confirmed: NIST agreement 70NANB15H044, pyincore 1.22.0 of 2025-07-31 (latest on PyPI and conda; 1.23.0 release candidates as git tags), MPL-2.0, conda install, pip unsupported and Linux-only, free account activated by an administrator. Rewritten 2026-09-26 by the r1 cross-cutting piece from the IN-CORE pages read that day; earlier links and routes kept.
